emitters.name: W1
emitters.notes_html:
Unmatched pencil-beam throw for its size: the pick for maximum reach from a small light. 1 mm² die, cool white (~6000K). The same package also comes in green, verdure, red, blue and orange (BLF Guide, Convoy Osram).

Green (~520 nm): saturated true green with high perceived brightness, popular for hunting and signalling.
Verdure (phosphor-converted lime/mint): centred near the eye's 555 nm sensitivity peak, so very high lumens per watt and a distinct "money green" tint.
Red (620 nm): red-orange that protects dark adaptation far better than white; for the most night-vision preservation, 660 nm deep red (e.g. SST-20-DR) is better.
Blue (~445 nm): short-wavelength blue thrower; Emisar/Noctigon also sell a W2 Deep Blue.
Orange (amber): warm monochrome for wildlife watching and cutting glare in fog and rain (Convoy Osram).

emitters.name: XP-G3

emitters.name: XT-E HE

emitters.tldr: A small, efficient lumen-optimised LED for small-cell lights.

emitters.name: XP-P

emitters.tldr: The domed XHP35.2: more lumens, less throw than the HI.

emitters.tldr: Cree's smallest lighting-class LED, common for aux and colour channels.

emitters.name: XD16

emitters.tldr: A tiny chip-scale Cree LED with a wide 135° spread.

emitters.name: XP-E2

emitters.tldr: The small-die domed classic of budget and AAA lights.

emitters.name: MK-R
emitters.notes_html: Cree's first 7 × 7 mm multi-die LED, the XHP70's ancestor; old builds only. Cree now points new designs to newer parts (Cree MK-R datasheet).
emitters.tldr: Cree's first 7 × 7 mm multi-die LED, the XHP70's ancestor; old builds only.

emitters.name: XHP35 (gen 1)

emitters.tldr: The original 12V-only XHP35, replaced by the 3V/6V XHP35.2.

emitters.name: XHP50 / XHP70 (gen 1)
emitters.notes_html: First-generation domed XHPs, superseded by the .2 and .3 parts. Same footprints and voltages, so later parts drop in. Floody, with a visible tint ring (BLF Guide).
emitters.tldr: First-generation domed XHPs, superseded by the .2 and .3 parts.

emitters.name: SST-90

emitters.tldr: The original big-die lumen part from the early 2010s.

emitters.name: SBT-90 (gen 1)

emitters.tldr: The first SBT-90: the domeless thrower that the SBT90.2 replaced.

emitters.name: CBT-90
emitters.notes_html: A projector-class 9 mm² chip that turns up in a few searchlights. Monolithic, 5700K / 6500K; green (over 1,800 lm) and blue versions exist (Luminus CBT-90 datasheet).
emitters.tldr: A projector-class 9 mm² chip that turns up in a few searchlights.

emitters.name: CFT-90
emitters.notes_html: A second-generation 9 mm² windowless specialty white. More peak lumens and current than the CBT-90; 5700K, 6500K or 7800K (Luminus CFT-90 datasheet).
emitters.tldr: A second-generation 9 mm² windowless specialty white.

emitters.name: CFT-50X
emitters.footprint_html: large-die package · 10 A CW (12.5 A pulsed)
emitters.notes_html: A 5 mm² windowless cool white with very high luminance for its size. Electrically isolated and designed for fibre coupling (Luminus CFT-50X datasheet).
emitters.tldr: A 5 mm² windowless cool white with very high luminance for its size.

emitters.name: SST-70X
emitters.notes_html: A newer 6V/12V configurable SST-70 with higher lumen density. Up to 500 lm/mm²; 6500K only (Luminus SST-70X datasheet).
emitters.tldr: A newer 6V/12V configurable SST-70 with higher lumen density.

emitters.name: SST-20F / SST-36F
emitters.notes_html: Luminus's cost-per-lumen flip chips in a ceramic package. SST-20F 3000–6500K at 65–80 CRI; SST-36F 2700K, 4000K, 5000K, 5700K and 6500K at 65–90 CRI, the 90 CRI bins in 2700K, 5700K and 6500K. Sometimes misspelled “SFT-36F”. The Acebeam Terminator M1 2.0 uses the SST-36F (Luminus SST-20F datasheet, Luminus SST-36F datasheet).
emitters.tldr: Luminus's cost-per-lumen flip chips in a ceramic package.

emitters.name: SST-20V
emitters.notes_html: A V-Line SST-20 with higher lumen density and a narrower emission angle. Vertical chip; the high-CRI version comes in 5000K / 5700K (Luminus SST-20V datasheet).
emitters.tldr: A V-Line SST-20 with higher lumen density and a narrower emission angle.

emitters.name: 757G / 757H
emitters.notes_html: Mid-power 3030s for lanterns and wide-angle work lights, not flashlight main emitters. Nichia's 0.2 W family (NFSW757G / NFSW757H / NF2W757H); the H6 series pairs Ra ≥ 95 with high efficacy (Nichia 757).
emitters.tldr: Mid-power 3030s for lanterns and wide-angle work lights, not flashlight main emitters.

emitters.name: NCSU276A / 276C
emitters.notes_html: An older, lower-power Nichia 365 nm UV, the one behind the Convoy S2+ UV. 276A, now 276C. Less output than the 233B, but a clean 365 nm peak with little visible purple (Nichia UV-A, Convoy S2+ UV).
emitters.tldr: An older, lower-power Nichia 365 nm UV, the one behind the Convoy S2+ UV.

emitters.name: NVSU119C
emitters.notes_html: Nichia's mid-power 365 nm UV-A emitter, a step below the 233B (1,450 mW). Listed alongside the 233B / 233C in Nichia's current UV-A range (Nichia UV-A).
emitters.tldr: Nichia's mid-power 365 nm UV-A emitter, a step below the 233B (1,450 mW).

emitters.name: P8
emitters.lm_html: ~250 lm each (2 × P8 = 500 lm in the TINI2 SS)
emitters.notes_html: Nitecore's name for the Osram emitter in the TINI2 SS keychain light. Two of them give 500 lm and 2,000 cd. Nitecore doesn't give the Osram order code (Nitecore TINI2 SS).
emitters.tldr: Nitecore's name for the Osram emitter in the TINI2 SS keychain light.

emitters.name: UHi 25
emitters.notes_html: Nitecore's in-house thrower die, between the UHi 20 and UHi 40. 2.26 mm² emitting surface, 4.7 SDCM colour tolerance, 6500K cool white (Nitecore EDC23 / EDC17 pages) (Nitecore EDC23).
emitters.tldr: Nitecore's in-house thrower die, between the UHi 20 and UHi 40.

emitters.name: M515S
emitters.lm_html: 1,000 lm / 380 m in the MT1C Max
emitters.notes_html: NiteLab's array LED, in the Nitecore P17iX / P27iX and MT1A / MT1C Max. Nitecore gives no CCT or CRI (Nitecore MT1C Max).
emitters.tldr: NiteLab's array LED, in the Nitecore P17iX / P27iX and MT1A / MT1C Max.

emitters.name: GT colour (red / green / blue)
emitters.notes_html: Single-colour Getian emitters for coloured throwers. Convoy sells them in red, green and blue for its throwers (C8, L21B, M21-series, 3X21A), and the green is a strong thrower. Buyers note a glass dome that cracks if the reflector is over-tightened (Convoy Getian).
emitters.tldr: Single-colour Getian emitters for coloured throwers.

emitters.name: LEP (laser-excited phosphor)
emitters.notes_html: Not an LED: a laser-lit phosphor dot for the narrowest, longest beams. A blue laser hits a phosphor dot, giving a tiny, extremely bright source. Output is low but candela is huge (often 300,000–1,000,000+ cd), so the beam is a narrow searchlight with almost no spill. Usually cool white; some lights add green or red LEP. Treat the beam like a laser around eyes and aircraft (FireflyLite LEP01).
emitters.tldr: Not an LED: a laser-lit phosphor dot for the narrowest, longest beams.

emitters.name: UV 365 nm (part not stated)
emitters.notes_html: For lights whose store page only says "365 nm UV". True 365 nm shows fluorescence with little visible purple, especially behind a ZWB2 filter; 395 nm parts are cheaper but wash scenes out in violet. Known named parts: Nichia 233B / 276A, Luminus SST-10-UV / SBT-10X-UV, Seoul CUN66A1B / CUN66A1G. Don't look into the beam (Nichia UV-A, Convoy UV).
emitters.tldr: For lights whose store page only says "365 nm UV".

emitters.name: KT CULPM1.13
emitters.notes_html: Osram's true-green projection LED, sold by Convoy as its "Verdure light" green. OSTAR Projection Compact: dominant wavelength 523–535 nm (typ. 530 nm) from a 1.5 × 1.2 mm² radiating surface, rated to 5 A. The 330–484 lm datasheet bins are at 1.4 A; driven harder it does far more (datasheet, Convoy).
emitters.tldr: Osram's true-green projection LED, sold by Convoy as its "Verdure light" green.

emitters.name: SFS-80
emitters.notes_html: A big-die 3535 San'an part, marked discontinued by the maker. Claimed ~2,000 lm and a '4000K 85 CRI' version, but a Kaidomain listing under the name 'P35 HI' may be a different emitter — the '4000K 80 CRI' sample there measured 5000K and under 70 CRI, quite green (BLF thread #50, BLF San'an thread, BLF Guide).
emitters.tldr: A big-die 3535 San'an part, marked discontinued by the maker.

emitters.name: SFS-75
emitters.notes_html: A large-die 3535 (bigger than the XP-L HI) claimed at 2,600 lm. Reportedly the SFS-80's replacement; no independent test yet (BLF thread #50).
emitters.tldr: A large-die 3535 claimed at 2,600 lm; no independent test yet.

emitters.name: SFQ-35
emitters.notes_html: Scant information: a small San'an-named die, presumably a throwier SFQ-43. It appears in San'an list posts but has no datasheet or test (BLF thread #50).
emitters.tldr: A small San'an-named die with no datasheet or test.

emitters.name: SFQ-43
emitters.notes_html: A very bright domeless 3535 San'an die, around XHP35.2 HI brightness. Used in the Mateminco MT18X; like most San'an parts it can be had in 3000K 90 CRI on request (BLF thread #50, BLF Guide).
emitters.tldr: A very bright domeless 3535 San'an die, around XHP35.2 HI brightness.

emitters.name: SFQ-46
emitters.notes_html: The SFQ-43 wired for 6V. Claims of over 3,000 lm; the suffix doesn't indicate a different die — it's the same array at higher voltage (BLF thread #50, BLF thread #59).

alternatives.name: SFQ-43
alternatives.why: The 3V version of the same part

emitters.tldr: The SFQ-43 wired for 6V.

emitters.name: SFS-72
emitters.notes_html: A San'an-named round-die 5050, very similar to the 'Yinding egg' emitter. Used in the Nightwatch NS14R (BLF thread #50).
emitters.tldr: A San'an-named round-die 5050, similar to the Yinding egg.

emitters.name: SSQ-55
emitters.notes_html: The domed version of the SFQ-55. Same dies as the SFQ-55; used in the Nightwatch NS14R (BLF thread #50).
emitters.tldr: The domed version of the SFQ-55.

emitters.name: SFQ-65
emitters.notes_html: A rarely-seen San'an-named 5050 around XHP50.3 HI brightness. Available in the Pioneman K75 (BLF thread #50).
emitters.tldr: A rarely-seen San'an-named 5050 around XHP50.3 HI brightness.

emitters.name: SFN-40
emitters.notes_html: A very bright San'an-named 5050; the cool-white variant reportedly has good tint. (BLF thread #50).
emitters.tldr: A very bright San'an-named 5050 with a decent cool-white tint.

emitters.name: SFH-35
emitters.notes_html: A 12V 3535 with 16 tiny dies — it looks like a waffle. Little documentation and now discontinued (BLF thread #50).
emitters.tldr: A 12V 3535 with 16 tiny dies, discontinued.

emitters.name: GT9090
emitters.notes_html: A cheap SBT90.2 clone: similar look, less performance, ~7000K, low CRI and greenish. Used in the NlightD T90v2; the BLF Guide groups it with the San'an-named parts, origin unclear (BLF Guide, BLF thread #50).

alternatives.name: SBT90.2
alternatives.why: The real thing: brighter and cleaner

emitters.tldr: A cheap SBT90.2 clone: less performance, ~7000K, low CRI and greenish.

emitters.name: L-90
emitters.notes_html: A very large round-die domeless emitter sold as 'L-90' — true name unknown. Similar to the old SBT-70 and the 'Yinding glass' parts, slightly less intense than an SBT-90; the glass lens can be removed to clean up the beam (BLF thread #50).
emitters.tldr: A very large round-die domeless emitter of unknown origin, sold as L-90.

emitters.name: Boost HL
emitters.notes_html: The 1 mm² Oslon Boost HL, sometimes called W2.1: a W1 on a 4040 pad, slightly brighter thanks to a bigger thermal pad. Marked discontinued and getting hard to find (BLF Guide, Dave's Oslon naming page).
emitters.tldr: The 1 mm² Oslon Boost HL (W2.1): a W1 on a 4040 pad, discontinued.

emitters.name: LUXEON V2
emitters.notes_html: An unrelated 3535 successor to the 4040 LUXEON V — and not an upgrade in beam quality. Brighter than the XP-G2/3 on paper, but tint-shiftier with lower CRI and output than a first-gen XP-L HI (BLF Guide, BLF thread #63).
emitters.tldr: A 3535 Lumileds emitter that under-delivers vs the XP-L HI.

emitters.name: LUXEON TX
emitters.notes_html: A small high-efficiency 3737 with a low Vf, used in many small Olights (i3E–i3T). Warm-white and high-CRI variants exist; decent tint aside from a strong blue spike (BLF Guide).
emitters.tldr: A small high-efficiency 3737 Lumileds emitter used in small Olights.

emitters.name: P70
emitters.notes_html: LatticePower's big flat 7070, comparable to a domeless XHP70. Up to ~4,000 lm when pushed; used in the Acebeam L35 (BLF Guide).
emitters.tldr: LatticePower's big flat 7070, used in the Acebeam L35.

emitters.name: UHe
emitters.notes_html: NiteLab's square-die high-output emitter, paired with UHi dies in Nitecore's 'MAX' arrays. (BLF Guide).
emitters.tldr: NiteLab's square-die high-output emitter, part of Nitecore's MAX arrays.

emitters.name: UHi Max
emitters.notes_html: Nitecore's flood-and-throw array: a central round UHi die ringed by small UHe dies. The outer dies switch together (wired in parallel, not separately) as a flood ring; the hollow-ring beam is why it divides opinion as a flood solution (BLF Guide, thread discussion).
emitters.tldr: Nitecore's central-UHi-plus-UHe-ring array for flood and throw.

emitters.name: Yuji 5mm
emitters.notes_html: The classic high-CRI 5 mm through-hole LED. A wide CCT range; reportedly discontinued along with the Sophia clone that briefly replaced it in Sofirn's C01 (BLF thread #62).
emitters.tldr: The classic high-CRI 5 mm through-hole LED.

emitters.name: Sophia 5mm
emitters.notes_html: A Chinese high-CRI 5 mm LED — the brief Yuji alternative in a Sofirn C01 batch, sold by rngwn. Reportedly discontinued (BLF thread #62, Sofirn C01 thread).
emitters.tldr: A Chinese high-CRI 5 mm LED, briefly used in the Sofirn C01.

emitters.name: 219C-V2
emitters.notes_html: A factory-domeless 219C for high-CRI throw, in the common 3535 pad. Listed at Kaidomain in 5700K R9050; enthusiasts await 4000–4500K bins (BLF thread #67, Kaidomain).
emitters.tldr: A factory-domeless 219C for high-CRI throw, currently only 5700K.

emitters.name: SFT-20
emitters.notes_html: A domeless mini-SST20 — but only as RGB. It has an offset emitting area and a non-standard 3535 pad (central pad joined to one side, so no electrically neutral thermal path) (BLF thread #50, BLF Guide).
emitters.tldr: A domeless mini-SST20, only made as RGB with an odd footprint.

emitters.name: Rayten 5050 Quad
emitters.section: 6. Boutique & House-Brand Emitters (FireflyLite FFL, Noctigon NTG, LMP, Getian, Convoy) — Other boutique / budget emitters
emitters.notes_html: A custom enthusiast-ordered quad round-die thrower that never materialised. Planned as R9070 ~4500K 3V, pitched against the SFT-40 (BLF Guide).
emitters.tldr: A custom enthusiast quad round-die thrower that never materialised.

emitters.name: YinDing 5050 Round
emitters.section: 6. Boutique & House-Brand Emitters (FireflyLite FFL, Noctigon NTG, LMP, Getian, Convoy) — Other boutique / budget emitters
emitters.notes_html: The flat round-die 'egg' LED behind the YinDing/LeiTeng/Rayten confusion. The white-surround 3000K version is 90 CRI, the glass-lens 3000K version is 70 CRI with higher output; Getian lists the gold configuration as PST30W, and Convoy's egg version is the LMP-made W5050SQ4. The round die gives a clean beam, but efficiency and max current lag the XHP35 HI and XP-L HI (BLF thread #19, BLF thread #50, BLF Guide).
emitters.tldr: The flat round-die "egg" LED sold under several names.

emitters.name: LeiTeng 5050 Round
emitters.section: 6. Boutique & House-Brand Emitters (FireflyLite FFL, Noctigon NTG, LMP, Getian, Convoy) — Other boutique / budget emitters
emitters.notes_html: A round-die 5050 with a silica protector over the die — greenish tint but good efficiency. Used in some Olight throwers; LeiTeng and Rayten appear to be the same seller (BLF thread #7).
emitters.tldr: A silica-protected round-die 5050, greenish but efficient.

emitters.name: Yinding 3535 Ronda
emitters.section: 6. Boutique & House-Brand Emitters (FireflyLite FFL, Noctigon NTG, LMP, Getian, Convoy) — Other boutique / budget emitters
emitters.notes_html: A 3535 round-die 'Ronda' with a very small emitting area, between the CSLNM1 and CSLPM1 in size. Rated 3.3 A with hopes of being overdrivable to 5 A; not used in any known light (BLF thread #7).
emitters.tldr: A 3535 round-die "Ronda" with a very small emitting area.
